complaint.title: [DEMO C050] Audit errors are visible but request payloads are missing
complaint.description: Cedar reports that execution errors appear in fresh audit rows, but request arguments and response bodies are missing, preventing incident investigation.

hypotheses.description: Probable cause for the observed missing request/response bodies is a payload-capture-disabled state on the canonical tool-executor record for Cedar, not a downstream dashboard-only copy gap. The affected executor log already shows audit_row_present=true, payload_storage_enabled=false, and null request/response payloads; public reference material matches that row shape when payload storage is disabled. This explains the missing payload visibility for the observed Cedar execution, but the supplied evidence does not identify who or what set that state.
assumptions: The public payload-storage behavior described in the knowledge record applies to this production environment.
Cedar's failures, backlog, and latency may be related to execution distress, but they do not by themselves explain why the canonical row shows payload_storage_enabled=false.
No supplied canonical record attributes the disabled payload-storage state to a specific actor or change event.

hypotheses.description: A provider-side failure may have contributed to Cedar's 500s, but it is not the best explanation for the missing payload fields. The same-time Maple record shows the provider was available and an unrelated read succeeded, which argues against a broad provider outage. This remains an alternative explanation for some Cedar execution failures, not for the payload omission mechanism itself.
assumptions: This alternative addresses Cedar's execution failures more than the missing-payload symptom.
No same-request upstream trace was supplied, so provider reachability for req-redacted-demo is unverified.

recommended_actions: Collect canonical config/decision telemetry for request_id=req-redacted-demo to determine why payload_storage_enabled was false; recommended action only, not executed.
Align executor, audit, and persistence telemetry by request ID before/during/after the incident window to distinguish disabled capture from delayed persistence; recommended action only, not executed.

Request a nearby healthy canonical execution that explicitly shows request/response payload capture, because the current Maple control only helps scope provider health; recommended action only, not executed.
Monitor Cedar-specific upstream error details separately from the payload-visibility issue, since underlying_error_code is null on the observed executor row; recommended action only, not executed.
Treat synthetic telemetry cautiously: partial reproduce/metrics results are incomplete and should not be used to prove absence of wider impact; recommended action only, not executed.
limitations: Synthetic telemetry is incomplete in places: reproduce and metrics evidence include partial results, so absence elsewhere is not proven.
No canonical record identifies the actor, configuration source, or timestamp that set payload_storage_enabled=false.
No same-request provider trace was supplied to confirm whether req-redacted-demo reached the provider.
No healthy control record with explicit payload completeness was supplied.
The history record is analogy only and does not prove the current cause.

findings.statement: For the affected Cedar execution, the canonical tool-executor log shows an audit row was written while request and response payloads were null and payload_storage_enabled was false.
Public reference material states that disabling payload storage preserves audit metadata while omitting new request and response content, matching the observed Cedar row shape.

Observed impact is severe but tenant-scoped in the supplied snapshot: Cedar had 435 failures out of 789 requests, 435 blocked business operations, queue depth 141, and p95 latency 1880 ms, while Maple had 0 failures out of 637 requests, queue depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.

A same-time Maple execution succeeded and reported same_provider_available=true, which is counter-evidence to a broad provider outage, but no supplied healthy control explicitly demonstrates complete payload capture.
The only deployment record supplied in the broader window is an unrelated support-dashboard release, weakening an in-window tool-executor regression explanation.

Delayed payload availability or a later persistence fill remains unverified because no canonical audit-pipeline write timestamps, later-filled payload records, or same-request provider traces were supplied; partial synthetic reproduce/metrics results cannot establish absence.
